candidates.statement: Check the temperature outside the day before so as to plan whether to wear a thick coat or a light coat.
context: Checking the day before going out

evidence_candidates.quote: I use it usually to check the temperature outside, especially like the day before. So like, I can plan whether I should wear my thick coat or my light coat.

candidates.statement: When it is super cold, skip cycling and take the bus instead.

evidence_candidates.quote: if it's like super cold, I might skip going through bicycle and just go through the bus, because it's like very cool to like cycle down.

candidates.statement: Check the rain forecast and make sure to have an umbrella when rain is forecast.

evidence_candidates.quote: and I also check for rains. So if it's if there is a weather forecast for rain. I I make sure I have my umbrella.

candidates.statement: On first opening the app, look at temperature and at tomorrow's chance of rain.

evidence_candidates.quote: 1st is usually temperature, and like the rain meter, like the chance of happening like a rain happening tomorrow. So yeah, those 2 things.

candidates.statement: Check next day's hour-by-hour temperature around the morning time before classes, i.e. the time actually going out.

evidence_candidates.quote: So I just like check like for the next day it gives my gives me like an hour by hour detail. So I check usually like, if if in in the morning time, you know, like before our classes, what what the temperature is around that time. So when I'm actually going out.

candidates.statement: Check precipitation chances, treating 25 percent or more as a good chance of rain.

evidence_candidates.quote: And what's the what's the precipitation chances? So that's like between one and 100 usually 25 plus is like a good chance of rain happening.

candidates.statement: The city is already filled in because of previous use and because opening from a Google link points to the current city.

evidence_candidates.quote: So I think if you have used weather.com previously, it like, has that city in build.

candidates.statement: Be warned by weather.com about severe weather events affecting his own city, and treat it as the first place to learn about important weather events.
context: Severe weather event in his city

evidence_candidates.quote: So so yeah, so if if it's happening for my city, I'll definitely notice it.
it will like warn me like, for example.

candidates.statement: The app provides a safety guide or resources to read during an extreme weather event.

evidence_candidates.quote: So but I'm I'm pretty sure that they have some sort of guide to like, you know. Make sure you're safe, or something, or like some resources that you can read up to.

candidates.statement: On receiving a typhoon alert, open the notification and check the severity and all the details provided.

evidence_candidates.quote: Well, I'll probably open the notification check. You know the severity and all the details that they have about the typhoon, you know, if usually these kind of warnings are also given by like local authorities, or like some sort of Government meteorological organization.

candidates.statement: Read what local authorities or the meteorological organization recommend (evacuate, seek shelter, stay inside, or just umbrella and raincoat) before acting.

evidence_candidates.quote: So you know, I'll read for what they recommend like, should I? Should I evacuate the city? Should I just seek shelter, not go outside or like, just carry a umbrella and a raincoat?

candidates.statement: Adjust the day's plan based on the severity and the information given in the warning.

evidence_candidates.quote: So yeah, it depends on the severity. And like what information they've given. And like, yeah, based on that, I'll adjust my day.

candidates.statement: As soon as a trip is decided, check historical data if available or future/monthly forecasts to get a good estimate of the expected weather.
context: Trip decided, often a couple of weeks ahead

evidence_candidates.quote: So yeah, I immediately. Once I find that I'll be going. I either check for historical data if it's available somewhere, or I check for future weather focus because it gives you focus. That's you know, I had like monthly forecast as well. So you at least have a good estimate of what the what the weather will be like.

candidates.statement: Check cloud coverage for trips and reconsider or cancel if it will be overcast (beach vacation, astronomical event).
context: Trip purpose sensitive to cloud cover

evidence_candidates.quote: if you're going for a beach vacation, let's say, and it's going to be super cloudy. Then, you know, you might need to reconsider, because usually people go there to enjoy sun.

candidates.statement: As the trip date approaches, look again because the forecast becomes more accurate and a few days before gives a final view.

evidence_candidates.quote: and then, as you approach the date, the weather, like the weather forecast, becomes usually more accurate. So like a few days before you can get like a final you know, see on what the situation would be like.

candidates.statement: Wait until about two or three days before the trip and then decide based on the final temperature.
context: Two or three days before the trip

evidence_candidates.quote: So yeah, you should probably wait till the end and then then decide, based on what the final temperature is like. Couple of days before.

candidates.statement: Plans to screenshot temperatures below zero and share them on social media.
candidates.modality: planning to do it very soon; not done yet
context: He comes from a place where it never goes below 0

evidence_candidates.quote: if it if if I do see like a weather where the temperature is showing below 0, I'll probably like screenshot it and share it on my social medias. But yeah, I haven't done it yet.

candidates.statement: Prefer a plain black or plain white background instead of the dull blue colour scheme.

evidence_candidates.quote: because, like the background, is like a dull blue, which I don't really like, you know, they could just make it plain black or plain white. And I would prefer that.

candidates.statement: Consider the paid ad-free tier only if daily use exceeds 20-30 minutes; at current short usage it is not required.

just because I'm not, I don't use it that often. It's not required.

evidence_candidates.quote: Yeah, so I do prefer Celsius. And and yes, it is Fahrenheit.

evidence_candidates.quote: So if I go to the main page it does have sections for like weather events, not necessarily in my city. But you know, like important weather events. Ha! Happening across the world. So it does show me that. And if I click on it, it opens like a news tab in weather.com.

candidates.statement: Prefer no notifications and keep weather.com notifications off.
